transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And... I don't know, I just feel like I'm somehow damaged now. It's like the competent person who got promoted just isn't really there anymore, and I don't know how to get her back.
You mentioned that work doesn't feel safe anymore; did something specific happen at your workplace that changed how you feel?

Yeah, there was. Um, I was working late at the office doing an overnight deployment... and there was a break-in. All of this has been going on since that night, which was about two years and four months ago now.
Do you find yourself having intrusive thoughts, memories, or dreams about the break-in that make you feel like you are reliving the event?

Yeah, I do. It doesn't take much to trigger it, honestly. Um, just hearing a badge scanner beep, or heavy footsteps in the hallway, or even getting a late-night deployment alert... it can suddenly put me right back in that office. My chest gets really tight, and the image of the guard on the floor just cuts through whatever I’m doing. It really does feel like I'm right back in that moment.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid certain places, people, or activities that remind you of that night?

Yeah, I do. Um, I've started trading shifts and pushing back on our release windows whenever I can. I also try to work from home a lot more now. And if I do have to go in, I always take the side entrance. Just... walking through that main lobby after dark makes me feel like I'm going to come apart. So, yeah, I do whatever I can to avoid it.
You mentioned feeling 'damaged' and that your former self isn't there anymore; do you find yourself feeling like you can no longer trust other people or that the world is completely dangerous?

Yeah, I mean... it's exactly that. I just can't shake the feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And because of that, yeah, I do feel like I'm somehow damaged now. It's hard to explain, but... it's like the competent person who earned that promotion just isn't really there anymore. I don't know if I think the entire world is completely dangerous, but my world definitely feels that way now, and it's really changed how I see myself.
Since that night, have you noticed that you are more easily startled by sudden noises or that you feel constantly on guard, like you're always watching for danger?

Yeah, I definitely feel constantly on guard now. Um, whether I'm on the train, or sitting in a meeting, or even just at lunch with my team, I find myself automatically clocking the exits. I'm always watching to see who is standing a little too close to me. And I usually keep one ear tuned to any noises out in the hallway instead of actually being fully present in whatever I'm doing. I just can't really turn that off.
